summary:
Abuja Federal Capital Territory has no territorial variation from Nigeria's national framework: the Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014 and the criminal provisions it reinforces apply in the capital as they do elsewhere in the country, and the national assessment carries that layer in full.

The territory's documented trans-specific killing is that of a 33-year-old transgender woman and TikTok creator known as Abuja Area Mama. BBC News reported on 9 August 2024 that her beaten and bruised body was found along the Katampe-Mabushi expressway in the Banex/Wuse II area of Abuja on Thursday 8 August 2024, hours after she posted a final video; she had previously expressed fear for her life.

The official response misgendered the victim. A police statement described her as "a man fully dressed in female clothing with no means of identification". The Abuja police chief, Benneth Igweh, ordered a "thorough and discreet" investigation.

No charge followed. The Dial reported in February 2025, six months after the killing, that no suspects had been charged despite the public commitment to investigate. A petition carrying nearly 6,000 signatures demanded that the murder be pursued as a hate crime.

For a trans visitor or resident in the capital, the case sets the expected official posture: a trans woman killed on a city highway, recorded in police language by her clothing rather than her identity, with no prosecution recorded months later.
tangentialFactors:
The killing drew a public campaign rather than a prosecution. The petition demanding a hate-crime investigation gathered nearly 6,000 signatures, and no charging decision is documented in its wake.

Civil-society attention in the capital concentrated on the police's own description of the victim, which framed a transgender woman as a man in women's clothing, rather than on the circumstances of the death.

The case is the only Abuja-specific trans homicide in the sourced record; the wider pattern of arrests, extortion and venue closures documented nationally is not broken down by state in the available material.
localsOnly:
Trans residents of Abuja have the same case as their reference point: a local creator with a public following was killed and left on a highway in the Banex/Wuse II area, and no one has been charged.

The police statement on her death is the documented official record of how a trans victim is described in the capital, and it used clothing to classify her.

Residents who report violence have no documented instance in the capital of a prosecution following a trans person's death, and the petition campaign is the only recorded civic response.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the FCT investigation ordered in August 2024 remains open, whether any suspect was identified, and whether the killing was recorded as a hate crime are unresolved in the sourced material.

The petition's delivery, any official response to it, and its outcome are not sourced.

No Abuja-specific by-law, directive or police order on transgender or cross-dressing matters was identified; the applicable rules are national.
